- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (sentiment > 0.33) — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral (sentiment ≤ 0.33) — model is overly conservative.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to short-term volatility, then undercorrects in subsequent periods.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in capturing true trend — model often misses early momentum shifts.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 3–5 days, model should adjust downward slightly to avoid overconfidence bias.
- If recent 3–5 day price moves are steep, reduce forecast magnitude by 5–10% to account for volatility decay.
- Sentiment-driven corrections: if sentiment > 0.67, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overestimation; if sentiment < 0.33, increase by 2–5% to compensate for underestimation.
